question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Open to more than one interpretation, not having one obvious meaning
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Ambiguous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ambiguous" means open to more than one interpretation; having a doubtful or unclear meaning. (अस्पष्ट / द्विअर्थी)

◦ Example: His ambiguous reply left everyone confused about his real intention.

• The definition given in the question — "not having one obvious meaning" — is the textbook definition of ambiguous.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Alchemy" — the medieval forerunner of chemistry, concerned with turning base metals into gold. (कीमियागरी)

• Option 2 "Amateur" — a person who does something as a hobby, not professionally. (शौकिया)

• Option 4 "Altercation" — a noisy argument or quarrel. (तीखी बहस)

NOTE

• Related words: ambiguity (noun), ambiguously (adverb), unambiguous (clear, having only one meaning).

• Do not confuse ambiguous (having more than one meaning) with ambivalent (having mixed or conflicting feelings).

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Doze
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Wake.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Doze" means to sleep lightly; to take a short nap. Its antonym is "wake", which means to stop sleeping / to rouse from sleep. (झपकी लेना का विलोम — जागना)

◦ Example: Grandfather began to doze in his chair, but he woke the moment the bell rang.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Snooze" is a synonym of doze (to have a short light sleep), not an antonym — a classic trap option.

• Option 1 "Cold" and Option 2 "Neglect" (to fail to care for) are unrelated to sleeping.

NOTE

• Synonyms of doze: nap, snooze, slumber, drowse, nod off.

• Antonyms of doze: wake, awaken, rouse, stir, get up.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

They are virtually unimpeachable in the (unbiased), invariably correct reading of a race.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. prejudiced.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Unbiased" means fair, impartial, free from prejudice. Its antonym is "prejudiced", meaning having a preformed, unfair opinion; partial. (निष्पक्ष का विलोम — पूर्वाग्रही)

◦ Example: A judge must be unbiased; a prejudiced judge cannot deliver justice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "captivity" (the state of being imprisoned) is a noun and does not fit the adjective slot.

• Option 2 "stranger" (an unknown person) is a noun, unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4 "ceasing" (stopping) is unrelated to fairness.

NOTE

• Synonyms of unbiased: impartial, neutral, objective, fair, disinterested.

• Antonyms of unbiased: prejudiced, biased, partial, one-sided, bigoted.

• Note that "unimpeachable" in the sentence means beyond doubt or reproach.

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. rescind.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "rescind", which means to revoke, cancel or repeal a law, order or agreement. (रद्द करना / निरस्त करना)

◦ Example: The government decided to rescind the controversial order.

• Spelling key: RE + SCIND (note the silent "c" after "s", as in science, scissors, scene).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "recind", "recsind" and "resind" are all misspellings — they drop or misplace the "sc" cluster.

NOTE

• Related forms: rescission (noun — the act of rescinding), rescindable (adjective).

• Synonyms: annul, repeal, revoke, cancel, retract, nullify. Antonym: enact, uphold, ratify.

question:
Select the word from the options which is similar in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

Well, you want an (argument)," he added, "come on then."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. explanation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Argument" here does not mean a quarrel; it carries the sense of a reason or set of reasons given in support of something — i.e., an explanation/justification. (तर्क / स्पष्टीकरण)

◦ Example: He put forward a strong argument (explanation) for his absence.

• Thus "explanation" is the closest word in meaning among the options.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "agreement" (harmony of opinion) is the opposite of an argument in the quarrel sense.

• Option 2 "enhancement" (an improvement or increase) is unrelated.

• Option 3 "capability" (the ability to do something) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Senses of "argument": (i) a disagreement/quarrel, (ii) a reason or line of reasoning — a justification/explanation.

• Related words: argumentative (fond of arguing), arguably (as can be shown by argument).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

The Federalists wished to/ make the central government/ as strong possible.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. as strong possible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct structure of comparison of equality is "as + adjective + as". The second "as" has been wrongly omitted, so "as strong possible" must be "as strong as possible".

◦ Correct: The Federalists wished to make the central government as strong as possible.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "The Federalists wished to" is correct — "wish + to + V1" is a standard infinitive structure.

• "make the central government" is correct — "make + object + adjective" (make it strong).

NOTE

• Fixed comparison patterns: as ... as (as soon as possible, as far as possible, as much as possible), so ... as (in negatives: not so good as), the same ... as.

• "As ... as possible" is a very common SSC-tested expression; both "as" words are compulsory.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

The query isn't (whether he will admit it, but when).
option_2: whether he will be admitting it or not, but when?
option_3: whether or nor he will admit it, but when?
option_4: whether he will admit it or not, but when?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No substitution required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The bracketed segment "whether he will admit it, but when" is already grammatically correct and idiomatic. The construction "The question/query isn't whether ..., but when ..." is a standard contrast structure, so no change is needed.

◦ Correct: The query isn't whether he will admit it, but when.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "whether he will be admitting it or not, but when?" — the future continuous "will be admitting" is unnecessary, and a question mark is wrong in a statement.

• Option 3 "whether or nor" is a spelling/word error for "whether or not".

• Option 4 adds "or not", which makes the clause clash with the contrasting "but when", and again wrongly ends with a question mark.

NOTE

• "Whether ... or not" is used when both alternatives are stated; when the contrast is with another wh-word (as here, "but when"), plain "whether" is correct.

• Remember: an embedded/indirect question inside a statement takes a full stop, not a question mark.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A person who believes in the equality of all people
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Egalitarian.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "egalitarian" is a person who believes in the equality of all people and supports equal rights and opportunities for everyone. (समतावादी)

◦ Example: As a true egalitarian, she opposed every form of caste and class discrimination.

• The word comes from the French "égal" meaning "equal".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Philologist" — a person who studies the history and structure of languages. (भाषाशास्त्री)

• Option 3 "Philodendron" — a tropical climbing houseplant, not a person at all.

• Option 4 "Philander" — to flirt or have casual love affairs (a verb).

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: misanthrope (one who hates mankind), philanthropist (one who loves and helps mankind), altruist (one who works selflessly for others), feminist (one who supports women's rights).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

This initiative has been sharply criticised as grossly inefficient and ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Counterproductive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Counterproductive" means having the opposite of the desired effect; doing more harm than good. It pairs naturally with "grossly inefficient" in a sentence of sharp criticism. (उल्टा असर करने वाला)

◦ Correct: This initiative has been sharply criticised as grossly inefficient and counterproductive.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Capricious" — changing suddenly, unpredictable/whimsical; describes behaviour, not the outcome of a scheme.

• Option 3 "Calumny" — a false and malicious statement (slander); it is a noun and cannot follow "and" after the adjective "inefficient".

• Option 4 "Canonical" — conforming to accepted rules or an authoritative list; carries no negative sense.

NOTE

• Parallelism rule: the blank must hold an adjective to match "inefficient". Only "capricious", "counterproductive" and "canonical" are adjectives, and only "counterproductive" fits the critical tone.

question: Select the wrongly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Alturistc.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Alturistc" is wrongly spelt. The correct spelling is "altruistic", meaning selflessly concerned for the well-being of others. (परोपकारी)

◦ Example: Donating his entire salary to the flood victims was an altruistic act.

• Spelling key: AL + TRU + IS + TIC (note the "tru" and the ending "-istic").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Unsavoury" (unpleasant, morally disagreeable), "Ethical" (morally right) and "Unconventional" (not following what is usual) are all correctly spelt.

• Note the British spelling "unsavoury"; the American form is "unsavory".

NOTE

• Related words: altruism (noun — selfless concern for others), altruist (a selfless person). Antonyms: egoistic, selfish, self-centred.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Debased
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Corrupted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Debased" means reduced in quality, value or moral character; degraded or corrupted. Its closest synonym is "corrupted". (भ्रष्ट / निम्नीकृत)

◦ Example: Cheap flattery had debased/corrupted the whole system of awards.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Amenable" — willing to agree or be persuaded; responsive.

• Option 2 "Unamenable" — not willing to agree; unresponsive.

• Option 4 "Aggrandize" — to increase the power, wealth or status of someone, which is the opposite direction of debasing.

NOTE

• Synonyms of debased: corrupted, degraded, adulterated, devalued, defiled.

• Antonyms of debased: elevated, purified, ennobled, upgraded.

• Historically "debase" was used of coinage — mixing precious metal with cheaper metal to lower its value.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

We cannot ______ a religion or a political party that ignores the rights of half the human race.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. forgive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Forgive" means to pardon or stop feeling angry about an offence. The sentence expresses moral disapproval: a religion or party that ignores the rights of half the human race (i.e., women) cannot be pardoned. (क्षमा करना)

◦ Correct: We cannot forgive a religion or a political party that ignores the rights of half the human race.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "disseminate" — to spread information widely; it does not fit "cannot ... a religion".

• Option 2 "desiccate" — to dry out completely (used of food/soil); completely unrelated.

• Option 3 "condemn" — to express strong disapproval; it reverses the intended sense, because "we cannot condemn" would mean we approve of such a religion or party.

NOTE

• "Cannot forgive" = strong condemnation, so Option 4 keeps the critical tone of the sentence.

• Related words: forgiveness (noun), forgiving (adjective), unforgivable (beyond pardon).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

They probably subsisted on insects and other small ______ invertebrates and perhaps even on aquatic vertebrates.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. terrestrial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Terrestrial" means relating to or living on land (the earth). The sentence contrasts small terrestrial invertebrates (land creatures) with "aquatic vertebrates" (water creatures), so "terrestrial" is the perfect fit. (स्थलीय / भूमि पर रहने वाला)

◦ Correct: They probably subsisted on insects and other small terrestrial invertebrates and perhaps even on aquatic vertebrates.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "skittish" — nervous and easily frightened (usually of horses or people).

• Option 2 "recluse" — a person who lives alone and avoids others; it is a noun, so it cannot modify "invertebrates".

• Option 3 "reverent" — showing deep respect; meaningless for invertebrates.

NOTE

• Habitat adjectives: terrestrial (land), aquatic/marine (water), arboreal (trees), aerial (air), amphibious (both land and water), extraterrestrial (outside the earth).

• Invertebrates lack a backbone (insects, worms); vertebrates possess one (fish, frogs, birds).

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

The (roof collapsing) in a roar of rock and rubble.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. roof collapsed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence as given has no finite verb — "collapsing" is only a participle, leaving the sentence incomplete. A finite past-tense verb is required, so "roof collapsed" makes it a complete sentence.

◦ Correct: The roof collapsed in a roar of rock and rubble.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "roof have collapsed" — "roof" is singular, so it needs "has", not "have".

• Option 2 "No correction required" is wrong because the original is a sentence fragment.

• Option 3 "roof was collapse" — after "was" we need "collapsing" or "collapsed" as a participle, never the base form "collapse".

NOTE

• Every complete sentence needs a subject + finite verb. Present participles (-ing) alone cannot serve as the main verb.

• Subject–verb agreement: singular subject → singular verb (The roof collapses/has collapsed); plural subject → plural verb (The roofs collapse/have collapsed).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Can you please help me to this project?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. help me to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "help" takes the preposition "with" when it is followed by a noun naming the task. So "help me to this project" must be "help me with this project".

◦ Correct: Can you please help me with this project?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Can you please" is a correct polite request form.

• "this project?" is correct — a question mark is right for a direct question.

NOTE

• Correct patterns with help: help + object + with + noun (help me with the work); help + object + (to) + V1 (help me carry / help me to carry the box); help in + V-ing (help in solving the problem).

• "Help me to this project" is unidiomatic in standard English.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To kill two birds with one stone
option_1: A work which needs tremendous efforts
option_2: To achieve two things with a single effort
option_3: The weak point in a person
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To achieve two things with a single effort.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to kill two birds with one stone" means to achieve two aims/objectives with a single action or effort. (एक पंथ दो काज)

◦ Example: By cycling to office he killed two birds with one stone — he saved money and stayed fit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 describes a Herculean/uphill task, not this idiom.

• Option 3 "the weak point in a person" is the meaning of "Achilles' heel".

• Option 4 "to accidentally hurt someone's feelings" relates to "to tread on someone's toes".

NOTE

• Similar efficiency idioms: "a double whammy" (two blows at once, negative), "two for the price of one".

• Other bird idioms: "a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush", "birds of a feather flock together", "the early bird catches the worm".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The duke had capacity, but his life was so ________ that what influence he had upon the king was for evil.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. lewd.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lewd" means crude and offensive in a sexual way; morally vulgar and debauched. It explains why the duke, in spite of his ability ("capacity"), influenced the king for evil. (अश्लील / लम्पट)

◦ Correct: The duke had capacity, but his life was so lewd that what influence he had upon the king was for evil.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "seditious" — inciting rebellion against the state; a seditious duke would be an enemy of the king, not merely a bad influence.

• Option 2 "scrumptious" — extremely tasty/delicious (used of food); absurd here.

• Option 4 "ambitious" — having a strong desire to succeed; it is not inherently evil and does not explain "for evil".

NOTE

• Synonyms of lewd: obscene, vulgar, indecent, licentious, debauched. Antonyms: decent, chaste, modest, pure.

• Note the sentence structure "so ... that", which expresses cause and effect.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

He belted two huge sixers, but / eleven to get of the last two / deliveries was a big ask.
option_1: eleven to get of the last two
option_4: He belted two huge sixers, but
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. eleven to get of the last two.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In cricket, runs are scored "off" a delivery, not "of" it. The segment therefore needs the preposition "off": "eleven to get off the last two deliveries".

◦ Correct: He belted two huge sixers, but eleven to get off the last two deliveries was a big ask.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "deliveries was a big ask." is acceptable — the singular verb "was" agrees with the notional singular subject "eleven (runs) to get", i.e., the target treated as one unit.

• "He belted two huge sixers, but" is correct.

NOTE

• "Of" shows possession/belonging (the roof of the house); "off" shows separation/movement away (he fell off the horse, runs scored off the bowler).

• "A big ask" is an idiom meaning a demanding requirement / a tall order.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the bracketed idiom in the given sentence.

Sure, fixing a flubbed decision isn't always (a piece of cake), but it's rarely impossible.
option_1: The family bond is closer than anything else
option_2: A task that can be accomplished very easily
option_4: Having no stand, shows favour at one time and unfavour at another
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A task that can be accomplished very easily.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a piece of cake" means something very easy to do; an effortless task. (बहुत आसान काम)

◦ Example: For a trained mechanic, changing a tyre is a piece of cake.

• In the sentence, "fixing a flubbed decision isn't always a piece of cake" means it is not always easy — which fits Option 2 perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 relates to "blood is thicker than water".

• Option 3 "a rare event" relates to "once in a blue moon".

• Option 4 describes a person who keeps changing sides — "to run with the hare and hunt with the hounds" / "a fair-weather friend".

NOTE

• Synonymous idioms of easiness: "as easy as ABC", "child's play", "a walk in the park", "a cakewalk", "a breeze".

• "Flubbed" means bungled or botched (done badly).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The dessert was many sweet for my tastes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. too sweet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Many" is used only with plural countable nouns (many books, many people); it can never modify an adjective like "sweet". The correct intensifier for an excessive degree is "too".

◦ Correct: The dessert was too sweet for my tastes.

• "Too + adjective + for ..." expresses more than the acceptable/desirable amount.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "too sweetly" — an adverb cannot follow the linking verb "was"; a predicative adjective is needed.

• Option 2 "more sweeter" is a double comparative — always wrong (either "sweeter" or "more sweet").

• Option 4 "No improvement" is wrong because "many sweet" is clearly ungrammatical.

NOTE

• Quantifiers: many + plural countable (many chairs); much + uncountable (much sugar); too/very + adjective (too sweet, very sweet).

• "Too" carries a negative sense (more than needed), while "very" is neutral intensification: "very sweet" (pleasantly) vs "too sweet" (unpleasantly).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Network security (1) ______ securing a network and protecting the user's information about (2) ______ is connected through that network. Over the network (3) ______ steal, the packets of data through sniffing and spoofing (4) ______, man in the middle attack, war driving, etc, and misuse the data for their (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. means.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a verb that defines the term "Network security". "Means" is used to give the sense or definition of something. (अर्थ होना)

◦ Correct: Network security means securing a network and protecting the user's information ...

• Note the structure "X means + V-ing" (means securing), which is standard for definitions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "calls" would need a different structure ("Network security is called ...").

• Option 2 "names" is used for giving a name to something, not for defining a concept.

• Option 4 "declares" means to announce formally; a concept cannot "declare" anything.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: "Network security" is a singular uncountable idea, so the singular verb "means" is correct.

• Useful definition patterns: "X means ...", "X refers to ...", "X is defined as ...", "By X we mean ..."

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Network security (1) ______ securing a network and protecting the user's information about (2) ______ is connected through that network. Over the network (3) ______ steal, the packets of data through sniffing and spoofing (4) ______, man in the middle attack, war driving, etc, and misuse the data for their (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. who.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank refers to persons — the users who are connected through the network — so the relative pronoun "who" (used for people) is correct.

◦ Correct: ... protecting the user's information about who is connected through that network.

• Here "who is connected through that network" is a noun clause acting as the object of the preposition "about".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "which" and 4 "that" are used for things/animals, not for people in this context.

• Option 3 "whose" shows possession (whose laptop is connected) and would need a following noun, which is absent here.

NOTE

• Relative/interrogative pronouns: who (subject — persons), whom (object — persons), whose (possession), which (things), that (persons or things in defining clauses).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Network security (1) ______ securing a network and protecting the user's information about (2) ______ is connected through that network. Over the network (3) ______ steal, the packets of data through sniffing and spoofing (4) ______, man in the middle attack, war driving, etc, and misuse the data for their (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. hackers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hackers" are people who gain unauthorised access to computer systems and data. Only hackers "steal the packets of data through sniffing and spoofing" over a network. (हैकर)

◦ Correct: Over the network hackers steal, the packets of data through sniffing and spoofing ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "labourers" (manual workers) and Option 3 "engineers" (who build and maintain systems) do not steal data over a network.

• Option 4 "smugglers" illegally move physical goods across borders, not data packets.

NOTE

• Cyber-security terms: sniffing (secretly capturing data packets), spoofing (faking an identity or address), man-in-the-middle attack (intercepting communication between two parties), war driving (searching for unsecured Wi-Fi networks from a moving vehicle), phishing (tricking users into revealing passwords).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Network security (1) ______ securing a network and protecting the user's information about (2) ______ is connected through that network. Over the network (3) ______ steal, the packets of data through sniffing and spoofing (4) ______, man in the middle attack, war driving, etc, and misuse the data for their (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. attacks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is part of a list of hostile techniques — "sniffing and spoofing attacks, man in the middle attack, war driving, etc." The parallel item "man in the middle attack" confirms that "attacks" is the right word. (हमले)

◦ Correct: ... through sniffing and spoofing attacks, man in the middle attack, war driving, etc.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "raids" refers to sudden physical assaults or police searches, not network intrusions.

• Option 3 "charges" means accusations or fees — irrelevant here.

• Option 4 "guards" means protectors, which is the opposite of what hackers do.

NOTE

• Parallelism is a key clue in cloze passages: match the missing word with the pattern of the other items in the same list ("man in the middle attack").

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Network security (1) ______ securing a network and protecting the user's information about (2) ______ is connected through that network. Over the network (3) ______ steal, the packets of data through sniffing and spoofing (4) ______, man in the middle attack, war driving, etc, and misuse the data for their (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. benefits.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Hackers steal data and "misuse the data for their benefits" — i.e., for their own advantage or profit. (लाभ)

◦ Correct: ... and misuse the data for their benefits.

• The possessive "their" before the blank shows the gain belongs to the hackers themselves.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "banes" means causes of ruin or distress — nobody misuses data for their own ruin.

• Option 3 "pleasure" is uncountable in this sense and is too weak; theft of data is done for gain, not enjoyment.

• Option 4 "hindrances" means obstacles, the opposite of what a criminal seeks.

NOTE

• Synonyms of benefit: advantage, gain, profit, plus point. Antonyms: loss, drawback, detriment, harm.

• Common collocations: "for personal benefit", "reap the benefits", "benefit from something".

question: The Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022 belongs to ______ Ministry of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Corporate Affairs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was introduced in the Lok Sabha by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. It amends the Competition Act, 2002, which regulates anti-competitive practices in India. (कॉर्पोरेट कार्य मंत्रालय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Bill introduced the concept of a deal value threshold (transactions above ₹2,000 crore must be notified to the CCI), shortened the merger approval timeline, and provided for a settlement and commitment framework.

• The Competition Commission of India (CCI) was established in 2003 (became fully functional in 2009) under the Competition Act, 2002, with its headquarters in New Delhi.

NOTE

• The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the older MRTP Act, 1969 (Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act), on the recommendation of the Raghavan Committee.

• The Ministry of Corporate Affairs also administers the Companies Act, 2013, the LLP Act, 2008 and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

question: The rules made for the Buddhist "Sangha" were written down in a book called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vinaya pitaka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Vinaya Pitaka contains the rules and regulations of monastic discipline framed for the Buddhist Sangha (the order of monks and nuns). (विनय पिटक — संघ के नियम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Tripitaka ("Three Baskets") are the sacred texts of Buddhism, written in Pali:

◦ Vinaya Pitaka — rules of discipline for monks and nuns.

◦ Sutta Pitaka — the discourses/sermons of the Buddha.

◦ Abhidhamma Pitaka — philosophical and psychological analysis of Buddhist doctrine.

• Milinda Panha ("Questions of Milinda") records the dialogue between the Indo-Greek king Menander (Milinda) and the monk Nagasena.

NOTE

• Buddhist Councils: 1st — Rajgriha (483 BCE, under Ajatashatru), 2nd — Vaishali (383 BCE), 3rd — Pataliputra (250 BCE, under Ashoka), 4th — Kashmir (under Kanishka).

• The Tripitaka was first written down in the 1st century BCE in Sri Lanka at the Aluvihara monastery.

question: Which among the following is NOT a bacterial disease?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabies.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rabies" is a viral disease, not a bacterial one. It is caused by the Rabies virus (Lyssavirus), transmitted mainly through the bite or saliva of an infected dog, and it affects the central nervous system. (रेबीज़ — विषाणुजनित रोग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Cholera — caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae, spread through contaminated water and food.

• Typhoid — caused by Salmonella typhi, spread through contaminated food and water.

• Plague — caused by Yersinia pestis, spread by rat fleas.

NOTE

• Other viral diseases: influenza, AIDS, dengue, chikungunya, polio, measles, mumps, chickenpox, COVID-19, hepatitis.

• Other bacterial diseases: tuberculosis, tetanus, diphtheria, leprosy, whooping cough, anthrax.

• The anti-rabies vaccine was developed by Louis Pasteur (1885); rabies is nearly 100% fatal once symptoms appear, but fully preventable by timely vaccination.

question: The bank rate in the Indian economy is determined by the ________ .
option_4: Securities and Exchange Board of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reserve Bank of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The bank rate — the rate at which the RBI lends long-term funds to commercial banks without collateral — is determined by the Reserve Bank of India, the country's central bank. (बैंक दर — भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, on the recommendation of the Hilton Young Commission; it was nationalised in 1949. Headquarters: Mumbai. First Governor: Sir Osborne Smith; first Indian Governor: C. D. Deshmukh.

• Key RBI rates: Repo rate (short-term lending to banks against securities), Reverse repo rate (RBI borrows from banks), Bank rate (long-term lending, no collateral), MSF (Marginal Standing Facility), CRR and SLR.

NOTE

• SEBI (1988; statutory in 1992) regulates the securities market, while the State Bank of India is only a commercial bank. Monetary policy rates are decided by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), a six-member body headed by the RBI Governor.

question: Preet writes about an ocean that separates North America from Europe. Which ocean is it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atlantic Ocean.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Atlantic Ocean lies between the Americas on the west and Europe and Africa on the east, so it is the ocean that separates North America from Europe. (अटलांटिक महासागर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Atlantic is the second largest ocean in the world (after the Pacific) and is shaped roughly like the letter "S".

• It contains the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, the longest mountain chain on earth, and the Bermuda Triangle.

• The Pacific Ocean (largest and deepest, containing the Mariana Trench) separates Asia from the Americas.

NOTE

• Five oceans: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern (Antarctic) and Arctic.

• The Indian Ocean is the only ocean named after a country; the Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest.

question: Which among the following is the highest peak of West Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sandakphu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sandakphu (about 3,636 m / 11,930 ft) is the highest peak of West Bengal. It lies in the Singalila Ridge of the Darjeeling Himalayas, on the border with Nepal. (सांदकफू — पश्चिम बंगाल की सबसे ऊँची चोटी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• From Sandakphu one can see four of the world's five highest peaks — Everest, Kanchenjunga, Lhotse and Makalu; it is popularly called the "Sleeping Buddha" viewpoint.

• Saramati is the highest peak of Nagaland; Doddabetta is the highest peak of the Nilgiris (Tamil Nadu); Deomali is the highest peak of Odisha.

NOTE

• Highest peaks: India — Kanchenjunga (8,586 m, Sikkim); world — Mount Everest (8,848.86 m); Western Ghats — Anamudi (Kerala).

question: All Indian Muslim league was formed at Dacca in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1906.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The All India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at Dacca (Dhaka) by Nawab Salimullah of Dhaka, along with Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk and Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk. (अखिल भारतीय मुस्लिम लीग — 1906, ढाका)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Its formation followed the Partition of Bengal (1905) by Lord Curzon and the Simla Deputation (1906) led by the Aga Khan to Viceroy Lord Minto.

• The Morley–Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act, 1909) granted separate electorates to Muslims.

• The Lucknow Pact (1916) brought about Congress–League unity; the League later adopted the Pakistan Resolution at Lahore in 1940.

NOTE

• Other key foundations: Indian National Congress (1885, by A. O. Hume), Hindu Mahasabha (1915), Ghadar Party (1913, San Francisco).

question: Dilwara Temples at Mount Abu, Rajasthan is an example of ______ temple architecture.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Dilwara Temples at Mount Abu, Rajasthan, are famous Jain temples, celebrated worldwide for their extraordinary marble carving. They were built between the 11th and 13th centuries CE. (दिलवाड़ा जैन मंदिर — माउंट आबू)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The complex has five temples; the most famous are the Vimal Vasahi temple (built 1031 CE by Vimal Shah, dedicated to the 1st Tirthankara Adinatha/Rishabhanatha) and the Luna Vasahi temple (1230 CE, by Vastupala and Tejpala, dedicated to the 22nd Tirthankara Neminatha).

• Mount Abu is the only hill station of Rajasthan, located in the Aravalli Range; Guru Shikhar is its highest point.

NOTE

• Other important Jain sites: Ranakpur temple (Rajasthan), Shravanabelagola (Karnataka — Gomateshwara/Bahubali statue), Palitana (Gujarat), Khajuraho Jain group (Madhya Pradesh).

question: Who among the following won the French Open 2022 Badminton Tournament Men's Doubles Title in Paris?
option_1: Chirag Shetty and Satwiksairaj Ranki Reddy
option_2: Lu Ching Yao and Yang Po Han
option_4: Ko Sung Hyun and Shin Baek Cheol
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chirag Shetty and Satwiksairaj Ranki Reddy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian pair Chirag Shetty and Satwiksairaj Rankireddy won the men's doubles title at the French Open (BWF Super 750) 2022 in Paris, becoming the first Indian pair to win a BWF Super 750 title. (चिराग शेट्टी और सात्विकसाईराज रंकीरेड्डी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The same pair won gold at the Commonwealth Games 2022 (Birmingham) and were part of India's historic Thomas Cup 2022 winning team.

• In 2023 they won the Asian Games gold, the Asia Championships, the Indonesia Open (Super 1000) and became World No. 1 in men's doubles.

NOTE

• Badminton is governed by the Badminton World Federation (BWF). Other Indian stars: P. V. Sindhu (Olympic silver 2016 and bronze 2020, World Champion 2019), Saina Nehwal, Lakshya Sen and H. S. Prannoy.

question: Which among the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the "Fundamental Duties"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 51-A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51-A in Part IV-A of the Constitution lists the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens. (अनुच्छेद 51-क — मौलिक कर्तव्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. Originally 10 duties were listed; the 11th duty (providing education to children aged 6–14) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

• They were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by the courts.

NOTE

• Other related Articles: Article 51 — promotion of international peace and security (a Directive Principle); Article 52 — the President of India; Article 53 — executive power of the Union.

question: "Losar" is celebrated as New year festival in Sikkim. It is celebrated on the first day of the first month of the ______ lunar calendar.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tibetan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Losar is the Tibetan New Year festival, celebrated on the first day of the first month of the Tibetan lunar calendar. In India it is celebrated in Sikkim, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh by Buddhist communities. (लोसार — तिब्बती नववर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Lo" means year and "sar" means new in Tibetan. The festival lasts about 15 days, with the first three days being the most important, and features masked Cham dances, prayer flags and family feasts.

• Other festivals of Sikkim: Pang Lhabsol, Saga Dawa, Bumchu, Losoong (Namsoong) and Maghe Sankranti.

NOTE

• New Year festivals across India: Ugadi (Andhra/Karnataka), Gudi Padwa (Maharashtra), Baisakhi (Punjab), Bihu (Assam), Puthandu (Tamil Nadu), Vishu (Kerala), Navreh (Kashmir), Cheti Chand (Sindhi).

question: In 2022, the Union Ministry of Electronics and IT approved the greenfield Electronic Manufacturing Cluster (EMC) in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2022, the Union Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) approved a greenfield Electronic Manufacturing Cluster (EMC 2.0) in Maharashtra (at Aurangabad/Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar), to boost domestic electronics manufacturing. (महाराष्ट्र — इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विनिर्माण क्लस्टर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The EMC 2.0 Scheme provides financial assistance for creating world-class infrastructure — common facility centres, ready-built factory sheds, power, water and logistics — for electronics manufacturing.

• A "greenfield" project is set up on entirely new, undeveloped land, whereas a "brownfield" project uses existing facilities or land.

NOTE

• Related schemes of MeitY: PLI (Production Linked Incentive) Scheme, SPECS (Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors), Digital India, India Semiconductor Mission and Make in India.

question: Dribbling is associated with ______ sport.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Basketball.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dribbling" — bouncing the ball continuously with one hand while moving — is a fundamental skill and term of basketball. (बास्केटबॉल — ड्रिबलिंग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Basketball was invented by Dr. James Naismith in 1891 at Springfield, Massachusetts (USA). A team has 5 players on court; the ball must be passed through a hoop 10 feet (3.05 m) above the floor.

• The world governing body is FIBA (Fédération Internationale de Basketball), founded in 1932, headquartered at Mies, Switzerland.

• Basketball terms: dribble, dunk, rebound, pivot, free throw, travelling, foul, three-pointer.

NOTE

• Dribbling is also used in football (soccer) and hockey, but among the given options only basketball is a dribbling sport; cricket, badminton and swimming have no dribbling.

question: Bhopal gas disaster occurred in which of the following factory?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Union Carbide Pesticide plant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bhopal gas tragedy occurred on the night of 2–3 December 1984 at the Union Carbide India Limited (UCIL) pesticide plant in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, when the highly toxic gas Methyl Isocyanate (MIC) leaked. (यूनियन कार्बाइड कीटनाशक संयंत्र — भोपाल गैस त्रासदी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It is regarded as the world's worst industrial disaster; thousands died immediately and lakhs suffered long-term health damage.

• The plant manufactured the pesticide Sevin (carbaryl), for which MIC was an intermediate.

• The disaster led to the enactment of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 and the setting up of the National Green Tribunal (2010).

NOTE

• 2 December is observed as National Pollution Control Day in India in memory of the Bhopal victims.

question: Which among the following is not associated with Tabla?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shakoor Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shakoor Khan was a celebrated sarangi player, not a tabla exponent. The other three names in the list are all associated with the tabla. (शकूर खान — सारंगी वादक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Jnan Prakash Ghosh — an eminent tabla maestro and guru of the Farukhabad gharana from Bengal, teacher of many famous percussionists.

• Sabir Khan — a distinguished tabla player of the Farukhabad gharana.

• Sandeep Das — a Grammy Award-winning tabla player, a disciple of Pandit Kishan Maharaj, who performed with the Silk Road Ensemble.

NOTE

• The tabla is a pair of drums (dayan/tabla played with the right hand and bayan/dagga with the left); its invention is traditionally attributed to Amir Khusrau.

• Famous tabla maestros: Ustad Zakir Hussain, Ustad Alla Rakha, Pandit Kishan Maharaj, Pandit Samta Prasad, Pandit Anindo Chatterjee.

• Tabla gharanas: Delhi, Ajrara, Lucknow, Farukhabad, Benaras and Punjab.

question: Yakshagana is a famous folk dance associated with which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Yakshagana is a traditional folk theatre-dance form of Karnataka, popular especially in the coastal districts (Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Uttara Kannada) and the Malenadu region. (यक्षगान — कर्नाटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Yakshagana combines dance, music, dialogue, elaborate costumes, towering headgear (kirita) and vivid make-up, and enacts episodes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas. Performances traditionally run through the night.

• The singer-narrator is called the Bhagavata; the main instruments are the chande (drum), maddale, harmonium and taala (cymbals).

NOTE

• Other folk dances: Bihu (Assam), Garba/Dandiya (Gujarat), Ghoomar/Kalbeliya (Rajasthan), Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Lavani/Tamasha (Maharashtra), Chhau (Jharkhand/Odisha/West Bengal), Theyyam (Kerala).

• Classical dance of Karnataka: Bharatanatyam is widely practised, but Yakshagana is its signature folk form.

question: Who occupied Badaun (A.D. 1197-98) and appointed Iltutmish as its first Muslim Governor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Qutbuddin Aibak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Qutbuddin Aibak occupied Badaun (A.D. 1197-98) and appointed Iltutmish as its first Muslim Governor. Iltutmish was Aibak's slave and later his son-in-law. (कुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक — बदायूँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Qutbuddin Aibak (r. 1206–1210) was a slave-general of Muhammad Ghori and the founder of the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. He began the construction of the Qutub Minar and built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque (Delhi) and the Adhai Din ka Jhopra (Ajmer).

• He was famous for his generosity and was nicknamed "Lakh Baksh" (giver of lakhs). He died in 1210 at Lahore after falling from a horse while playing Chaugan (polo).

• Iltutmish (r. 1211–1236) shifted the capital to Delhi, completed the Qutub Minar, introduced the silver tanka and copper jital, and set up the Turkan-i-Chahalgani (Corps of Forty).

NOTE

• Dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate: Slave/Mamluk (1206–90), Khalji (1290–1320), Tughlaq (1320–1414), Sayyid (1414–51), Lodi (1451–1526).

question: What is another name for frozen carbon dioxide?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dry Ice.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Solid (frozen) carbon dioxide is commonly called "dry ice". It is called "dry" because it does not melt into a liquid — it sublimes, changing directly from solid to gas at about –78.5 °C at normal atmospheric pressure. (शुष्क बर्फ — ठोस कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Uses of dry ice: refrigerated transport of food, ice cream and vaccines, creating fog/smoke effects on stage, and cloud seeding for artificial rain.

• Sublimation is the direct conversion of a solid into vapour; other subliming substances are camphor, naphthalene, iodine and ammonium chloride.

NOTE

• Coke is a solid fuel obtained by the destructive distillation of coal; coal is a fossil fuel; a refrigerant (like Freon/ammonia) is any working fluid used in a cooling system — none of these is frozen CO₂.

question: What is the official language of Bangladesh, a neighbouring country of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bengali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bengali (Bangla) is the official and national language of Bangladesh. (बांग्ला — बांग्लादेश की राजभाषा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bangladesh: capital Dhaka, currency Taka, national anthem "Amar Sonar Bangla" (written by Rabindranath Tagore). It became independent from Pakistan in 1971.

• 21 February is observed as International Mother Language Day by UNESCO, commemorating the Bengali Language Movement of 1952.

• India shares its longest land border (about 4,096 km) with Bangladesh, touching West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

NOTE

• Official languages of neighbours: Bhutan — Dzongkha; Pakistan — Urdu (and English); Nepal — Nepali; Sri Lanka — Sinhala and Tamil; Myanmar — Burmese; Afghanistan — Pashto and Dari; Maldives — Dhivehi.

question: Which among the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for the Attorney General of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 76.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 76 of the Constitution provides for the Attorney General of India, who is the highest law officer of the country and the chief legal adviser to the Government of India. (अनुच्छेद 76 — भारत का महान्यायवादी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Attorney General is appointed by the President and must be qualified to be a judge of the Supreme Court. He holds office during the pleasure of the President and has the right of audience in all courts in India.

• He can participate in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament and their committees (Article 88) but has no right to vote.

• India's first Attorney General was M. C. Setalvad.

NOTE

• Other Articles: Article 72 — pardoning power of the President; Article 79 — constitution of Parliament; Article 81 — composition of the Lok Sabha; Article 165 — Advocate General of a State.

question: Which of the following reforms led to the enactment of the Government of India Act of 1919?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Montagu- Chelmsford reforms.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms (proposed by Edwin Montagu, Secretary of State for India, and Lord Chelmsford, the Viceroy) led directly to the enactment of the Government of India Act, 1919. (मॉन्टेग्यू-चेम्सफोर्ड सुधार — भारत शासन अधिनियम 1919)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Key features of the Act of 1919:

◦ Introduced "Dyarchy" (dual government) in the provinces — subjects were divided into Transferred (handled by ministers responsible to the legislature) and Reserved (handled by the Governor and his council).

◦ Introduced bicameralism at the Centre — the Council of State and the Legislative Assembly.

◦ Extended separate electorates to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans.

◦ Provided for the appointment of a statutory commission after 10 years — which came as the Simon Commission (1927).

NOTE

• The Morley–Minto Reforms produced the Indian Councils Act, 1909 (separate electorates for Muslims); the Young Bengal Movement was a 19th-century reform movement led by Henry Vivian Derozio.

question: Which is the second largest family in modern Indian languages?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dravidian (Dravida).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among modern Indian languages, the Dravidian (Dravida) family is the second largest, spoken by roughly 20% of the population, after the largest family — the Indo-European (Indo-Aryan) group. (द्रविड़ भाषा परिवार — दूसरा सबसे बड़ा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The four major language families of India:

◦ Indo-European (Aryan) — about 73% of speakers: Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Odia, Assamese, Sanskrit.

◦ Dravidian (Dravida) — about 20%: Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Tulu, Gondi.

◦ Austro-Asiatic (Austric/Nishada) — about 1.4%: Santhali, Mundari, Khasi.

◦ Sino-Tibetan (Kirata) — about 0.9%: Manipuri (Meitei), Bodo, Naga languages.

NOTE

• Classical languages of India include Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Telugu and Kannada (2008), Malayalam (2013) and Odia (2014) — four of these six belong to the Dravidian family.

• The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution currently recognises 22 languages.

question: Lacchu Maharaj was a noted Indian classical dancer and choreographer of ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lacchu Maharaj (Baijnath Prasad) was a renowned Indian Kathak dancer and choreographer of the Lucknow gharana. (लच्छू महाराज — कथक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He choreographed dances for classic Hindi films such as Mughal-e-Azam and Pakeezah, and he belonged to the illustrious family of Kathak exponents that also produced Achhan Maharaj, Shambhu Maharaj and Birju Maharaj.

• Kathak originated in North India (Uttar Pradesh) and derives its name from "Katha" (story) — the storytellers or Kathakars. It is marked by fast footwork (tatkar), pirouettes (chakkars) and expressive abhinaya.

• Kathak gharanas: Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam). Chhau is a semi-classical/folk martial dance.

question: What chemical element does "H" stand for in the periodic table of science?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hydrogen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the periodic table, the symbol "H" stands for Hydrogen, the first element (atomic number 1) and the lightest and most abundant element in the universe. (हाइड्रोजन — प्रतीक H)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Hydrogen was discovered by Henry Cavendish (1766) and named by Antoine Lavoisier (Greek: "hydro" = water, "genes" = forming).

• Its isotopes are protium (¹H), deuterium (²H) and tritium (³H).

• Hydrogen is placed in Group 1, Period 1; it is used in the Haber process for ammonia, in hydrogenation of oils (vanaspati ghee) and as a clean fuel (green hydrogen).

NOTE

• Symbols of the other options: Helium — He (atomic number 2), Mercury — Hg (from Latin hydrargyrum, atomic number 80), Holmium — Ho (atomic number 67).

• India launched the National Green Hydrogen Mission in January 2023.

question: 'I Too Had a Love Story' novel is written by ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ravinder Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "I Too Had a Love Story" (2008) is the debut novel of the Indian author Ravinder Singh. It is a semi-autobiographical love story that became a bestseller. (रविंदर सिंह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other books by Ravinder Singh: Can Love Happen Twice?, Like It Happened Yesterday, Your Dreams Are Mine Now, This Love That Feels Right.

• Aravind Adiga wrote "The White Tiger", which won the Man Booker Prize in 2008.

• Ruskin Bond wrote "The Room on the Roof" (John Llewellyn Rhys Prize), The Blue Umbrella and A Flight of Pigeons; he received the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan.

• Durjoy Datta wrote "Of Course I Love You" and "She Broke Up, I Didn't!".

NOTE

• Indian Booker winners: Arundhati Roy — The God of Small Things (1997), Kiran Desai — The Inheritance of Loss (2006), Aravind Adiga — The White Tiger (2008); Geetanjali Shree — Tomb of Sand (International Booker, 2022).
